title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Stocks remain in correction territory heading into Monday after Friday's AI-led rout — Nasdaq -5.3% (worst week in over a year, now negative for 2026), S&P 500 -3.7%, Dow -949 pts (-1.9%); S&P and Dow are both down more than 10% from recent peaks.

Markets: Investors fled to safety Friday — the 10-year Treasury yield sank to 4.909% and the 2-year to 4.611%, the bond market's best week since 2024 — while gold still fell 4.6% to a 52-week low of $3,512/oz and Brent crude slipped 3.4% on the week to ~$92.57.

Companies: Nvidia shares are down more than 10% since CEO Jensen Huang's Nov. 12 resignation, and the WSJ reports the SEC has opened a civil inquiry into the company's disclosures; interim CEO Colette Kress is running the business while a search firm seeks a permanent replacement.

Companies: Anthropic's newly listed shares gave back their first-day pop, dipping as low as $83.05 (just above the IPO price) as AI-infrastructure names (Sandisk, Bloom Energy, Nvidia, semis) took the sharpest hits; the PHLX Semiconductor index fell ~11% Friday alone.
Companies: Recent M&A still being digested: Marvell's ~$115B all-stock bid for Lumentum, Fox's ~$22B deal for Roku, and CVS Health's plan to split into two public companies.
Macro/Policy: Prediction markets have flipped toward a 25bp Fed rate HIKE at the Dec. 9 meeting rather than a cut, reversing earlier bets after hotter-than-expected inflation data.

Macro/Policy: Week ahead: October PCE inflation (the Fed's preferred gauge), new home sales, Case-Shiller home prices, earnings from Dell, Best Buy, Dollar Tree and Deere, and a Dec. 1 congressional hearing tied to the Nvidia/Huang probes.
